text: Can I attack a gunboat with spears (in melee)?
answer: No. Gunboats may neither melee attack nor be melee attacked (7.1).

text: Can my gunboat fight in melee?
answer: No. Gunboats have no melee strength and may not melee attack (7.1).

text: Can I melee from two hexes away?
query: RETURN rule:r7_2_adjacent.statement CONTAINS "adjacent enemy units only";
answer: No. Units may melee attack adjacent enemy units only (7.2).

text: Can I assault over the wall?
answer: No. Units may not melee attack across a wall hexside, only through a gate or breach hexside (7.2).

text: My battalion was destroyed in the melee. Does it still hurt the attacker?
query: RETURN rule:r7_3_simultaneous.statement CONTAINS "still get a melee combat die roll";
answer: Yes. Melee is simultaneous, so units eliminated by melee attacks still get their melee combat die roll (7.3).

text: Who rolls first in a melee?
answer: It doesn't matter: melee combat is considered simultaneous (7.3).

text: Can my artillery melee attack?
answer: No. Only infantry, cavalry, camel units and Dervish leaders may melee attack (7.4).

text: Can the Maxims melee attack?
answer: No. The Maxim battery is not infantry, cavalry, camel or a Dervish leader (7.4).

text: Can artillery defend in melee?
answer: Yes. All units except gunboats may melee defend (7.4).

text: Can the Khalifa attack in melee?
answer: Yes. Dervish leaders may melee attack (7.4, 6.51).

text: Can Kitchener melee attack?
answer: No. Only Dervish leaders are named among melee attackers; Anglo-Egyptian leaders have a movement factor only (7.4, 6.51).

text: Infantry charges my Lancers. Can I get away?
answer: Yes. Cavalry may retreat two hexes from an infantry melee attack (7.5).

text: Can I retreat from a cavalry charge?
answer: No. The retreat is allowed only from an infantry melee attack (7.5).

text: My camels retreated and got attacked again. Can they retreat again?
answer: No. Only one retreat per unit per turn is permitted; enemy units whose attacks are not yet resolved may attack them where they retreated to (7.5).

text: Does retreating happen before or instead of rolling?
answer: The manual does not say: 7.5 allows the two-hex retreat from an infantry melee attack but gives no timing, and does not say whether either side still rolls (7.5).
note: Part B's bracketed answer 'Instead of fighting' overclaims; 7.5 does not say the retreat replaces the melee die rolls.

text: My Hadendowa killed all the defenders. Do I have to move in?
answer: Yes. If a melee attack eliminates all defenders in the hex, the Dervish player MUST advance into it (7.6).

text: Can I leave one unit behind after the forced advance?
answer: No. All surviving eligible Dervish units must advance, up to the stacking limit (7.6).

text: Can my British battalions decline to advance after a successful melee?
answer: Yes. The Anglo-Egyptian player may advance if desired; it is not compulsory (7.6).

text: Can the defender advance after a failed attack?
query: RETURN rule:r7_6_attackers_only.statement CONTAINS "Only attacking units may advance";
answer: No. Only attacking units may advance (7.6).

text: Does a forced advance pull my units out of good terrain?
query: RETURN [rule:r7_6_dervish_must_advance.params.all_must_advance, count(SELECT id FROM rule WHERE exception_to CONTAINS rule:r7_6_dervish_must_advance)];
answer: Yes. Every surviving eligible Dervish unit must advance, and 7.6 makes no exception for the terrain the attackers stand in (7.6).
note: Part B adds 'which is the point'; the manual states the obligation but not the designer's intent.

text: Does the defender roll too?
query: RETURN rule:r7_7_resolution.statement CONTAINS "attacker and defender both roll";
answer: Yes. Both the attacker and the defender roll on the Combat Results Table, each with its melee modifier (7.7).

text: Does hut terrain help me in melee?
query: RETURN count(SELECT id FROM rule WHERE exception_to CONTAINS rule:r7_7_no_terrain AND concerns CONTAINS terrain:hut) > 0;
answer: No. No terrain modifiers apply to melee; the only exception is Zariba hexsides (7.7, 9.23).

text: What's the Dervish melee bonus?
answer: +2 to the Dervish melee die roll (7.7).

text: Melee losses: do I pick from the whole stack?
expect: Melee losses must be taken from meleeing units first.
answer: No. Melee losses must be taken from the units that took part in the melee first (7.7).

text: Which CRT column do I use in melee?
answer: The manual does not say. Melee strength is printed on the counter (7.1) and both sides roll on the Combat Results Table (7.7), but which column a melee uses is not stated.
note: Part B's 'Your melee strength' is a reading, not stated in the manual; recorded as open_question:melee_crt_column.

text: Does the trench help defenders in melee?
answer: Yes. Dervish units melee attacking an entrenched unit get −2 instead of +2 (7.7 exception, 9.232).

text: Is my Dervish movement halved at night?
answer: No. Only Anglo-Egyptian movement allowances are halved at night; a 12-MP Dervish camel unit keeps 12 (8.1).

text: What is my 15-MP cavalry's movement allowance at night?
answer: 7: Anglo-Egyptian movement allowances are halved, rounding down (8.1).

text: Can my artillery fire at full range at night?
answer: No. All fire ranges are halved at night for both sides, rounding down (8.1).

text: Spears are range 1. Do they still work at night?
answer: Yes. Range 1 stays range 1 at night (8.1).

text: Which turns are night turns?
query: SELECT VALUE n FROM turn WHERE night = true ORDER BY n;
answer: Turns 9, 10, 19 and 20, the shaded NIGHT boxes of the Turn Record Track (8, TurnTrack).

text: Do Maxims get a second fire at night?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:night) CONTAINS action:maxim_second_fire;
answer: Yes, nothing forbids it: night removes only Anglo-Egyptian howitzer fire, and Maxim fire is subject only to the halved ranges (8.1).

text: When do my warriors run off (desert)?
query: RETURN { turn: (SELECT VALUE n FROM ONLY turn WHERE special = "Dervish Desertion Roll" LIMIT 1), phase: (SELECT VALUE out.name FROM ONLY allowed_in WHERE in = action:desert LIMIT 1) };
answer: During the movement phase of the first night turn of the campaign game, turn 9 on the track (8.2, TurnTrack).

text: I rolled a 4 for desertion. How many go?
answer: Six: deserters equal 1½ times the roll (8.2).

text: Can I choose to lose my worst units?
answer: Yes. The Dervish player chooses which units desert (8.2).

text: Can I lose a leader to desertion?
answer: Yes. Only the KHALIFA, gunboats, artillery units and forts may not be chosen, so other leaders may (8.2).

text: Does the British player score for deserters?
answer: No. No victory points are awarded for deserting Dervishes (8.2).

text: Does desertion happen in Fall of Khartoum too?
answer: No. The roll is made 'once each campaign game' (8.2).

text: Can the Dervish use both mines and chain?
answer: It isn't forbidden, but using both optionals in the same game is not recommended (10).

text: Does the British player know which optional rule is in use?
query: RETURN rule:r10_one_or_other.statement CONTAINS "without the Anglo-Egyptian player knowing which";
answer: Ideally not: the suggested use is that the Dervish has one or the other and the Anglo-Egyptian player finds out only when he stumbles onto it (10).

text: My gunboat was just ordered to stop. What happened?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM rule WHERE string::starts_with(section.num, "10") AND statement CONTAINS "must stop";
answer: It struck a mine: the Dervish player orders it to stop and rolls for the blast (10.12). With the chain option instead, a British gunboat entering a chained hex must also stop (10.22).
note: Part B answers only 'A mine'; the chain (10.22) also stops a British gunboat.

text: Can my mine-damaged gunboat still shoot?
query: SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:mine_damaged;
answer: Yes. The damage costs it its engines (it drifts); guns and Maxims are unaffected unless they drift out of range (10.12).

text: Does a mine-sunk gunboat give the Dervish 10 VP?
answer: Yes. The Dervish player gets 10 points for each British gunboat sunk, however it was sunk (9.14, 10.12).

text: Can both mines be in one hex?
answer: No. The two mines may not both be placed in the same hex (10.11).

text: After both mines have gone off, are there more?
query: RETURN rule:r10_13_two_only.statement CONTAINS "no more are available";
answer: No. After both mines have been rolled for, no more are available (10.13).

text: Can my Dervish gunboats sail through the mined hexes?
answer: Yes, with no ill effect; the Dervish player knows where the mines are (10.14).

text: Can my Dervish gunboats cross the chain?
answer: No. No gunboat, British or Dervish, may cross the chain until the British player has sunk it (10.23).

text: How do I get rid of the chain?
query: RETURN { artillery_min: threshold:sink_chain.min_result, units: (SELECT VALUE in FROM capability WHERE out = action:sink_chain AND allowed = true ORDER BY in) };
answer: Either an infantry or cavalry unit spends one complete turn on a riverbank adjacent to a chained hex, or artillery fires at the chain and gets 3 or more on the CRT (10.23).

text: Can a gunboat's own artillery shoot the chain?
answer: Only by reading: gunboats fire an artillery factor, so the corpus records it as implied, but 10.23 says only 'artillery' and the manual never says whether gunboats count (open_question:artillery_meaning).
note: Part B's 'Artillery fire is allowed, so yes' overclaims: whether 'artillery' includes gunboats is open (open_question:artillery_meaning); the corpus records the edge as implied.

text: How long can the chain be?
answer: Not more than four river hexes (10.21).

text: Who was the Mahdi, and why is his tomb worth 25 points?
query: RETURN { mahdi: person:mahdi.name, tomb_vp: location:mahdis_tomb.vp, why: location:mahdis_tomb.description };

expect.why: not only the tallest structure in the entire Sudan in 1898, it was also a Dervish holy shrine

answer: Mohammed Ahmed Ibn Al-Sayid Abdullah proclaimed himself the Mahdi, the Messiah, in 1881 (11). His tomb was the tallest structure in the Sudan and a Dervish holy shrine, so it is worth 25 VP (9.14).

text: Who are the 'Fuzzy-Wuzzies'?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM tribe WHERE aka CONTAINS "Fuzzy-Wuzzies";
answer: The Hadendowa, Osman Digna's troops, who broke Baker Pasha's square and later a British square (11).

text: Why do the named gunboats have howitzers?
answer: The new shallow-draft gunboats of 1898 carried 12-pounders, 6-pounders and Maxims on the upper deck and 4-inch howitzers on the gun deck (11).
note: Fails until unit_class:named_gunboat carries the section 11 history (see needs file).

text: Why are there 17 forts?
answer: To guard the approaches to Omdurman the Khalifa had seventeen forts built and armed with old artillery pieces (11, 9.111).
note: Fails until unit:fort carries the section 11 history (see needs file).

text: Why do only the Jehadia and Danagla have rifles?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM tribe WHERE history CONTAINS "Remingtons";
answer: The few guns available, old Remingtons and brass muzzle loaders, were issued to the Jehadia and the Danagla; the rest carried swords and spears (11).
note: Part B's 'only' slightly overclaims: the Isa Zachneih unit also fires on the rifles line (2.31).

text: Why is there a gap in Khartoum's wall?

expect.gap: washed away by the receding White Nile after the flood

answer: The receding White Nile had eroded a section of the wall; some 20,000 Dervishes poured through it on 25 January 1885 (11, 2.1).

text: Who commands the Jehadia?
answer: Sheik El Din, the Khalifa's son (11, 5.53).

text: What happened to the 21st Lancers?
answer: They won their first battle streamer and three Victoria Crosses in one of history's last great knee-to-knee cavalry charges (11).

text: D on a stack of 3. How many flip?
answer: Two: half the units in the target hex, rounded up, are disrupted (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: The result is '2' but the hex has 1 unit. What happens?
answer: The unit is eliminated; what, if anything, happens to the excess loss is not stated (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: My modifiers bring the roll to −1. Is that an automatic miss?
answer: No. Modified die rolls below 1 are treated as 1 (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: Can I roll above 10 with bonuses?
answer: No. Modified die rolls above 10 are treated as 10 (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: My unit got disrupted in his defensive fire. Can it melee this turn?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINS action:melee_attack;
answer: No. Disrupted units may not melee, and they turn face up only at the end of your player turn (Disrupted Units).
note: The query asks whether the disrupted state prohibits melee attack (true = it may not melee).

text: When does a disrupted unit recover?
expect: turned face up at the end of the owning player's turn
answer: At the end of the owning player's (your) player turn it is turned face up (Disrupted Units).

text: Can a disrupted unit defend in melee?
answer: Not settled: the back cover says disrupted units 'may not melee', while 7.4 says all units except gunboats may melee defend (Disrupted Units, 7.4).

text: If my unit is disrupted during the enemy's turn, is it still disrupted for my next movement?
query: RETURN { recovery: state:disrupted.recovery, may_move: (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINSNOT action:move };

expect.recovery: turned face up at the end of the owning player's turn

answer: Yes. It turns face up only at the end of your own player turn, so it sits out your movement phase and recovers at the end of that turn (Disrupted Units).

text: Can a disrupted unit hold the Tomb?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINS action:occupy_tomb;
answer: No. The British leader and the combat unit taking the Tomb must both be undisrupted at the conclusion of play (9.14).
note: true = the disrupted state prohibits taking the Tomb.

text: Can a disrupted unit be disrupted again?
query: SELECT VALUE kind FROM open_question WHERE refs CONTAINS state:disrupted AND question CONTAINS "already disrupted";
answer: The manual does not address it: a D disrupts half the units in the hex, rounded up, and says nothing about units that are already disrupted (Explanation of Combat Results, Disrupted Units).
note: Fails until the corpus records this gap as an open_question (see needs file).

text: It's turn 8 (8:00 pm). Is the next turn night?
answer: Yes. Turn 9, the next box, is the first NIGHT turn (Turn Record Track).

text: When's the desertion roll?
query: SELECT VALUE n FROM turn WHERE special = "Dervish Desertion Roll";
answer: Turn 9, the first night turn, marked 'Dervish Desertion Roll' on the track (Turn Record Track, 8.2).

text: It's turn 15. What time is it?
answer: 2:00 pm on 2 September 1898 (Turn Record Track).

text: It's turn 8 (8:00 pm). How many turns until dawn?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE n FROM turn WHERE n > 8 AND night = false ORDER BY n LIMIT 1)[0] - 8;
answer: Three: turns 9 and 10 are night, and turn 11 is 6:00 am on 2 September (Turn Record Track).

text: What is the Anglo-Egyptian melee modifier?
answer: +1 to the Anglo-Egyptian melee die roll (7.7).

text: Can cavalry melee attack?
answer: Yes. Infantry, cavalry, camel units and Dervish leaders may melee attack (7.4).

text: Can the Camel Corps melee attack?
answer: Yes. Camel units may melee attack (7.4).

text: Can a Baggara unit melee attack?
answer: Yes. Dervish tribal units are infantry, and infantry may melee attack (7.4).

text: Can a fort melee attack?
answer: No. A fort's melee value is defensive only (6.54, 7.4).

text: Can a fort be melee attacked?
answer: Yes. All units except gunboats may melee defend; a fort defends with its melee value (7.4, 6.54).

text: Which units can retreat from a melee?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM capability WHERE out = action:retreat AND allowed = true;
answer: Cavalry and camel units, from an infantry melee attack (7.5).

text: Can my Danagla camels retreat from an infantry melee attack?
answer: Yes, two hexes (7.5).

text: Can infantry retreat from a melee attack?
answer: No. Only cavalry and camel units are given a retreat (7.5).
note: Implied: 7.5 is the only retreat in the rules. The corpus has no edge for other units, so fn::allowed returns NONE (see needs file).

text: Which units are eligible to advance after a melee?
expect: participated in the melee attack that eliminated the defenders
answer: Units that were adjacent to the vacated hex and took part in the melee attack that eliminated the defenders (7.6).

text: How many units can advance into the vacated hex?
answer: Up to the stacking limit, four units (7.6, 5.51).

text: Can I melee attack through a gate or breach?
query: RETURN rule:r7_2_walls.statement CONTAINS "may melee attack through a gate or breach hexside";
answer: Yes. Melee is barred across a wall hexside but allowed through a gate or breach hexside (7.2).

text: Are terrain modifiers applied to melee?
query: RETURN rule:r7_7_no_terrain.statement CONTAINS "No terrain modifiers apply to melee combat";
answer: No, except Zariba hexsides in the historical scenario and, if constructed, the campaign game (7.7).
note: true = the corpus records that no terrain modifiers apply.

text: What melee modifier do the Friendlies use?
answer: +2: the Friendlies melee with the Dervish melee modifier (6.52, 7.7).

text: What is the 21st Lancers' melee strength?
answer: 5, printed on the counter (8·5·15) (7.1, 2.3).

text: What melee strength does 32 Battery defend with?
answer: 1, printed on the counter (10·1·7); artillery may defend but not attack in melee (7.1, 7.4).

text: Is melee the last phase of my player turn?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM phase WHERE player_turn_phase = phase:ae_player_turn ORDER BY step DESC LIMIT 1;
answer: Yes. Melee attacks come after movement and fire combat, at the end of the player turn (4, 7).

text: Is turn 10 a night turn?
answer: Yes. Turn 10 (SEPT. 2 NIGHT) is a shaded night box (Turn Record Track).

text: What time is turn 13?
answer: 10:00 am on 2 September (Turn Record Track).

text: How many night turns are in the campaign?
query: RETURN count(SELECT id FROM turn WHERE night = true);
answer: Four: turns 9, 10, 19 and 20 (Turn Record Track).

text: Are there night turns in the historical scenario?
answer: No. It runs from 6:00 am to 12:00 noon on 2 September, all day turns (9.22).

text: Is turn 1 of Fall of Khartoum a night turn?
answer: Yes. Turn 1 is always a night turn there, with the effects of 8.1 (9.341).

text: Can the gunboats fire their howitzers at night?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:night) CONTAINS action:howitzer_fire;
answer: No. There is no Anglo-Egyptian howitzer fire on night turns (8.1, 6.64).

text: At night, can my British infantry fire at range 3?
answer: No. At night Anglo-Egyptian infantry may not fire at range 3 or more (8.1).

text: At night, is my infantry still doubled at range 1?
answer: Yes. Range effects are the same as by day: doubled at range 1, normal at range 2 (8.1).

text: How far does a range-5 weapon reach at night?
answer: 2 hexes: ranges are halved and rounded down (8.1).

text: How far does a range-3 weapon reach at night?
answer: 1 hex: half of 3 rounded down (8.1).

text: What is an old gunboat's downstream allowance at night?
answer: 8: all Anglo-Egyptian movement allowances are halved at night, gunboats included (8.1, 5.24).

text: How far can an 8-MP Egyptian battalion move at night?
answer: 4 movement points: half of 8 (8.1).

text: Can the Khalifa desert?
answer: No. The KHALIFA unit may not be chosen to desert (8.2).

text: Which Dervish units can't be chosen to desert?
answer: The KHALIFA unit, gunboats, artillery units and forts (8.2).

text: Can a Hadendowa unit desert?
answer: Yes. Any Dervish unit except the KHALIFA, gunboats, artillery and forts may be chosen (8.2).

text: Can Dervish artillery desert?
answer: No. Artillery units may not be chosen (8.2).

text: I rolled a 10 for desertion. How many units desert?
answer: Fifteen: 1½ × 10 (8.2).

text: I rolled a 2 for desertion. How many units desert?
How many desertion rolls are there per campaign game?
answer: One, on the first night turn (8.2).

text: Is there a desertion roll in the historical scenario?
answer: No. The roll is made once each campaign game (8.2).

text: What happens on a mine roll of 6?
expect: gunboat damaged: lost use of its engines, drifts two hexes per turn with the current for the rest of the game
answer: The gunboat is damaged: it loses its engines and drifts two hexes per turn with the current for the rest of the game (10.12).

text: What happens on a mine roll of 9?
answer: The gunboat is sunk (10.12).

text: What happens on a mine roll of 3?
answer: No effect (10.12).

text: How many river mines does the Dervish player get?
Where may the mines be placed?
expect: south of the E–W hexrow in which the Khor Shambat empties into the Nile
answer: In Nile River hexes south of the E–W hexrow in which the Khor Shambat empties into the Nile (10.11).

text: Can the optional rules be used in the historical scenario?
answer: No. The optional rules are for the campaign game only (10).

text: How far does a mine-damaged gunboat drift?
answer: Two hexes per turn, for the rest of the game (10.12).

text: Which way does a damaged gunboat drift?
answer: With the current, i.e. downstream (10.12).

text: What happens when my gunboat enters a chained hex?
expect: A British gunboat entering a chained river hex must stop and may move no further that turn.
answer: It must stop and may move no further that turn (10.22).

text: My artillery got a 2 against the chain. Is it sunk?
answer: No. Artillery needs 3 or more on the Combat Results Table to sink the chain (10.23).

text: Can my cavalry sink the chain?
answer: Yes, by spending one complete turn on a riverbank adjacent to a chained hex (10.23).

text: Can my British gunboats cross the chain before it is sunk?
answer: No. No gunboat may cross the chain until it has been sunk (10.23).

text: When did the Mahdi proclaim himself?
When did Khartoum fall?
answer: In the pre-dawn hours of 25 January 1885 (11).

text: What scenario recreates 25 January 1885?
query: RETURN array::flatten(SELECT VALUE ->appears_in->scenario FROM historical_event WHERE date = "1885-01-25");
answer: The bonus game FALL OF KHARTOUM (11, 9.3).

text: When did the Mahdi die?
answer: In June 1885 (11).

text: Who succeeded the Mahdi?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM person WHERE role CONTAINS "succeeded the Mahdi";
answer: The Khalifa, Abdullah the Taiasha, a chief of the Baggaras (11).

text: When did Kitchener arrive at Kerreri?
answer: On 1 September 1898, where the campaign game begins (11, 9.1).

text: When was the Battle of Omdurman?
answer: 2 September 1898; by 11:30 it was virtually over (11).

text: Who commanded Kitchener's Egyptian Division?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM person WHERE role CONTAINS "Egyptian Division";
answer: General Hunter (11).

text: What was Kitchener's title?
answer: Sirdar, commander of the Egyptian army (11, 1.1).

text: Who was captured at the Atbara?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM person WHERE role CONTAINS "Atbara";
answer: Mahmud, one of the Khalifa's few remaining competent generals (11).

text: Whose army was destroyed at Kashgeil?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM person WHERE role CONTAINS "Kashgeil";
answer: Hicks Pasha's Egyptian army, on 4 November 1883, about 225 miles southwest of Khartoum (11).

text: When did the Mahdi invest Khartoum?
What did Queen Victoria write in her diary about Gordon?
expect: The government alone is to blame
answer: After Khartoum fell: 'The government alone is to blame'; after Omdurman: 'Surely now he is avenged' (11).

text: When was Kitchener's memorial service for Gordon?
answer: On 4 September 1898, two days after the battle, before the ruins of the palace in Khartoum (11).

text: What does a D result do?
expect: ½ (round up) of the units in the target hex are disrupted (inverted).
answer: Half the units in the target hex, rounded up, are disrupted (inverted) (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: What does a '—' result mean?
answer: A miss, no effect (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: What does a number result on the CRT mean?
expect: That many units in the target hex are eliminated, i.e. removed from play.
answer: That many units in the target hex are eliminated, removed from play (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: A D hits a hex of four units. How many are disrupted?
answer: Two, half of four (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: A D hits a lone unit. Is it disrupted?
answer: Yes: half of one rounded up is one (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: What bonus does the CRT give Anglo-Egyptian direct fire?
answer: +1 on all Anglo-Egyptian direct fire attacks (Explanation of Combat Results, 6.24).

text: What is the brigade integrity bonus?
answer: +1 (Explanation of Combat Results, 5.54).

text: Can a disrupted unit move?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINS action:move;
answer: No. Disrupted units may not move (Disrupted Units).
note: true = the disrupted state prohibits movement.

text: Can a disrupted unit fire defensively?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINS action:defensive_fire;
answer: No. Disrupted units may not fire offensively or defensively (Disrupted Units).

text: Does a disrupted unit have a ZOC?
query: RETURN (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINS action:exert_zoc;
answer: No. Disrupted units have no ZOC (Disrupted Units, 5.41).
note: true = the disrupted state removes the ZOC.

text: How do I mark a disrupted unit?
answer: Invert the counter (Explanation of Combat Results).

text: What date and time is turn 1 of the campaign?
answer: 6:00 am, 1 September 1898 (Turn Record Track).

text: When is the last turn of the campaign game?
answer: Turn 22, 8:00 am on 3 September (Turn Record Track, 9.12).

text: Which turn is noon on 2 September?
query: SELECT VALUE n FROM turn WHERE date = "1898-09-02" AND time = "12:00";
answer: Turn 14 (Turn Record Track).

text: How many turns does the campaign game last?
answer: 22 turns, the whole Turn Record Track (Turn Record Track, 9.12).

text: How much time does a day turn represent?
answer: Two hours; the track steps from 6:00 am to 8:00 pm in two-hour boxes (1.2, Turn Record Track).

text: Which section 7 rules govern melee attacks?

answer: 7.1 (printed strength, no gunboats), 7.2 (adjacent only, not across walls), 7.3 (simultaneous), 7.4 (who attacks) and 7.7 (resolution, no terrain modifiers, losses).

text: Which unit states prohibit melee attacks?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM prohibits WHERE out = action:melee_attack;
answer: Disrupted units (back cover), units constructing the Zariba (5.3) and Royal Engineers performing demolitions (6.53).

text: Which rules are exceptions to 'no terrain modifiers in melee'?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM exception_to WHERE out = rule:r7_7_no_terrain;
answer: The Zariba hexsides: thorn hedge (no melee across) and trench (Dervish −2 instead of +2) (7.7, 9.231, 9.232).

text: Which actions take place in the Dervish melee phase?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM allowed_in WHERE out = phase:d_melee;
answer: Melee attack and defence, cavalry/camel retreat, and advance after melee (7.4, 7.5, 7.6).

text: Which actions does the disrupted state prohibit?
query: SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted;
answer: ZOC, movement, all fire and melee (back cover), Royal Engineers' demolition (6.53) and taking the Tomb (9.14).

text: Which rules concern night turns?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM concerns WHERE out = state:night;
answer: 8.1's three effects (movement, howitzers, ranges), 6.64 (no howitzer fire at night) and 9.341 (FALL OF KHARTOUM turn 1 is night).

text: What turn comes after turn 9?
answer: Turn 10, the second night box (SEPT. 2 NIGHT) (Turn Record Track).

text: It's turn 18. What will the box two turns later say?
answer: Turn 20, 'SEPT. 3 NIGHT' (Turn Record Track).

text: Which historical event does the historical scenario recreate?
answer: The Battle of Omdurman on 2 September 1898 (11, 9.2).

text: Which historical events are recreated by a scenario?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM historical_event WHERE count(->appears_in) > 0;
answer: The fall of Khartoum (FALL OF KHARTOUM), Kitchener's arrival at Kerreri (campaign game) and the battle itself (historical scenario) (11).

text: Which persons of the historical notes have a counter in the game?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM person WHERE counter != NONE;
answer: The Khalifa, Gordon, Kitchener, Hunter, Osman Digna and Sheik El Din (11, 2.3, 9).

text: Which actions do the river chain rules govern?
query: RETURN array::distinct(SELECT VALUE out FROM governs WHERE in.section.num IN ["10.21", "10.22", "10.23"]);
answer: Recording the chain (10.21), gunboat movement into a chained hex (10.22), crossing it, and sinking it by units or artillery fire (10.23).

text: If I melee one hex from two different hexes, is it one combined attack or two?
answer: The manual doesn't say. 7.7 only says both sides roll on the CRT with their melee modifier; how attackers from several hexes are combined, and which column is used, is not stated.

text: Does the defender also have to take melee losses from its meleeing units first?
answer: Unclear. 7.7 says 'melee losses must be taken from meleeing units first' without saying whether this binds a defending stack, all of which defends, or only attackers with stackmates that did not attack.

text: Can a retreating cavalry unit pass through enemy ZOCs, and can the attacker advance into the hex it left?
answer: Not stated. 7.5 gives only the distance (two hexes), the trigger (an infantry melee attack) and the once-per-turn limit.

text: Does the corpus forbid disrupted units to melee defend?
query: RETURN { open: open_question:disrupted_melee_defense.kind, defend_prohibited: (SELECT VALUE out FROM prohibits WHERE in = state:disrupted) CONTAINS action:melee_defend };
answer: No: it records the question as open. The back cover says disrupted units 'may not melee', which clearly bars melee attack; 7.4 says all units except gunboats may melee defend.

text: I rolled a 7 for desertion: do 10 or 11 units desert?
answer: The manual doesn't say. 1½ × 7 is 10½, and 8.2 gives no rounding rule.

text: Does a gunboat drifting into a mined hex set the mine off?
answer: Not stated. 10.12 triggers a mine 'when a British gunboat enters a mined hex' and does not say whether drifting counts, or whether a damaged gunboat can trigger the second mine.

text: Is the 'one complete turn' to sink the chain a full game turn or one Anglo-Egyptian player turn?
answer: The manual says only 'one complete turn' on a riverbank adjacent to a chained hex (10.23).

text: Do leaders count toward the stacking limit that caps the compulsory Dervish advance?
answer: Not stated. 7.6 caps the advance at the stacking limit, and 5.51 lets leaders stack free, but 7.6 doesn't say how leaders are treated.

text: How does an infantry melee attack destroy a fort?
answer: 6.54 says forts may be destroyed by infantry melee attack and points to 7.6, but 7.6 says nothing about forts.

text: Can a D result disrupt an Anglo-Egyptian leader or a fort?
answer: Not stated. A D disrupts half the units in the hex; whether leaders and forts can be among them (which matters for the Tomb) is not said.

text: What exactly is my artillery's range at night?
answer: 8.1 halves ranges (round down, range 1 stays 1), but the day ranges are on the Range Effects Table, which is not in the manual text.

text: Which Dervish units count as cavalry or camels for the 7.5 retreat?
answer: Only the sample Danagla camel counter is identified in the text; the other Dervish units' types are on the counters (7.5, 2.3).
